title: Mutant Menace — Upgrade Options
summary: The Wise Mothman puts +1/+1 counters on creatures whenever nonland cards are milled from any library, and its rad counters make every player mill each turn. A shared removal package fixes the stock list's thin interaction; each direction then spends 6 more swaps on one plan. Budget: up to €20 per deck in total (Cardmarket prices).

notes: Curve shape is fine for a 4-mana commander, but several 2-drops (Power Fist, Nuka-Nuke Launcher, Biomass Mutation) don't affect the board.
Lumbering Megasloth (MV 12) and Agent Frank Horrigan (MV 7) are the clunkiest cards at the top.
Mana is fine: 39 lands + ~8 ramp. Many lands enter tapped (Temples, Opulent Palace, Tainted lands); improving them is a separate project.
Biggest weakness: only 5 spot removal and just 2 instant-speed answers.

core.name: Core interaction package
core.description: Four cheap instants that go in whichever direction you choose. Spot removal goes from 5 to 9, with 6 at instant speed.

swaps.why: Instant: destroy any permanent an opponent controls, for 2 mana. Megasloth costs 12 minus the counters in play, which you can rarely make cheap.
Kill a creature, or remove 3 counters from one. Biomass is a combat trick that mostly duplicates what your counters already do.
Instant: destroy any permanent; its controller gets a 3/3. Bobblehead is a 3-mana rock whose counter ability is slow.
Flexible: destroy a monocoloured creature, an artifact or an enchantment, or draw 2 and discard 1. Theta fits the theme but needs crewing; this was the closest cut.

directions.name: Counter Engine
directions.pitch: Mill every opponent every turn and turn each mill into +1/+1 counters. Ruin Crab and Mindcrank make rad counters and combat damage mill again; Kami and Evolution Sage grow everything further; Evolution Witness and Struggle for Project Purity keep the cards coming; Radstorm stays as a proliferate finisher.
directions.plays_like: Big creatures attacking; draws lots of cards

swaps.why: Each land you play mills each opponent 3. Simultaneous mills trigger Mothman once, counting every nonland card milled, so that's counters on about 6 creatures per land drop. Acolyte's ward 1 is a small effect.
+1 extra counter on every placement, and it taps for mana equal to its power, so Mothman's counters turn it into a big mana source. Power Fist needs equip mana and a successful hit.
Whenever it gets +1/+1 counters (Mothman does that constantly), return a permanent card from your graveyard to your hand. Repeatable card advantage. The Launcher's equip 3 is too expensive.

Proliferates on every land drop: more +1/+1 counters on your creatures and more rad counters on opponents. Watchful Radstag only copies itself when a bigger creature enters; Mothman's counters don't count.

Whenever an opponent loses life, they mill that many cards. Rad-counter mills already cost life, so every rad mill and every combat hit mills again, and each mill is another Mothman trigger. Piper only does anything when she deals combat damage.
Land swap. Untapped green or blue on its own. Overflowing Basin can't make mana by itself ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. Untapped black or green on its own. Viridescent Bog can't make mana by itself ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. Untapped blue or black. Temple of the False God only makes colourless mana, and only with five lands out.

how_to_play.summary: Make every player mill every turn. Each mill puts +1/+1 counters on your creatures, so your board grows until you win in combat or by emptying their libraries.

sections.title: How Mothman and rad counters work
points: Mothman: when it enters or attacks, each player gets a rad counter. Whenever nonland cards are milled, put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to X creatures (X = nonland cards milled). Several players milling at once triggers Mothman once, counting all of them.

Rad counters: at the start of each player's first main phase they mill one card per rad counter, lose 1 life per nonland card milled and remove one rad counter per nonland card. Milled lands don't remove counters.

sections.title: Turns 1–3: mill sources and ramp
points: Ruin Crab: each land you play mills every opponent 3.
Mindcrank: whenever an opponent loses life, they mill that many, so rad life loss and combat damage mill again.
Ramp: Talismans, Farseek, Rampant Growth.

sections.title: Turn 4: Mothman
points: Every player's rad mill now triggers Mothman, on every player's turn.
Spread counters, evasive creatures first: Mothman (flying), Nightkin Ambusher, Infesting Radroach.

sections.title: Keeping rad counters going
points: Engines: Evolution Sage proliferates on every land drop and Inexorable Tide on every spell. Protect them.

Attack triggers: Mothman (each player +1) and Screeching Scorchbeast (each player +2) when they attack. Hitting a player: Glowing One (+4), Infesting Radroach (+damage dealt), Vexing Radgull (+2 or proliferate).
Bursts: Nightkin Ambusher (+4), The Master and Mirelurk Queen (+2), Vault 12 (each player +3), Nuclear Fallout (+X each), Feral Ghoul on death, Bloatfly Swarm when damaged.
When you proliferate, add to opponents and skip yourself unless you want the mill.

sections.title: Engines and card draw
points: Boosters: Hardened Scales, Kami of Whispered Hopes, Winding Constrictor; doublers: Corpsejack Menace, Branching Evolution.
Struggle for Project Purity (choose Brotherhood): about 3 cards each upkeep. Opponents drawing is fine; you're milling them out anyway.
Mirelurk Queen, Marcus, Guardian Project; Evolution Witness returns a permanent from your graveyard each time it gets counters.
Fraying Sanity: curse the opponent who mills the most; they mill again at end of turn, which is another Mothman trigger.

sections.title: Your turn and tips
points: Rad mills happen at the start of your first main phase, so counters arrive before combat. Play your land before combat (Ruin Crab, Evolution Sage), then attack with Mothman.
You get rad counters too: watch your library and life, especially with Harold and Bob, Tato Farmer and Contaminated Drink. Strong makes you gain life from radiation instead.
Nuclear Fallout gives each creature −2X/−2X; your counter-loaded creatures often survive.
Use the instant-speed removal (Assassin's Trophy, Beast Within, Sultai Charm) at the end of an opponent's turn or in response to a threat.
Mulligan hands without 3+ lands and some ramp; you want Mothman on turn 4.

directions.name: Mill Them Out
directions.pitch: Empty opponents' libraries while their rad counters drain their life. Mothman's counters give you a combat plan as backup.
directions.plays_like: Quiet early, then decks the table

swaps.why: Each land you play mills every opponent 3.
A second land-mill Crab. Power Fist does nothing for a mill plan.

Every time an opponent mills, they mill 4 more, and its activated ability mills each opponent your hand size. A budget Bruvac ($3 instead of $41). Harold and Bob gives you rad counters, the wrong direction.
Each card you draw mills an opponent 2, and it repeats if the milled cards share a colour. Radstag is inconsistent.
Each card you draw mills every opponent 2. Strong irradiates you, the opposite of this plan.
{1}{B}: each player mills a card. Every creature card that hits a graveyard pings each opponent for 1. Mill and damage in one card. Frank is strong but costs 7.

how_to_play.summary: Empty opponents' libraries while their rad counters drain their life; Mothman's counters are the combat backup plan.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Ruin Crab and Hedron Crab: each land you play mills 3 (every opponent and one player respectively).
Draw-to-mill: Sphinx's Tutelage (each card you draw mills an opponent 2, repeating on shared colours) and Psychic Corrosion (each card you draw mills each opponent 2).
The Water Crystal: every opponent mill becomes mill +4. Syr Konrad: {1}{B} makes each player mill a card and pings opponents when creature cards hit graveyards.

sections.title: Tips
points: Prioritise card draw: every card you draw is a mill with the Tutelages.
Target the opponent with the smallest library first; one empty library means one player can't draw.
Keep enough blockers: this version wins slowly and doesn't race well.

directions.name: Graveyard Value
directions.pitch: Mill yourself on purpose, then replay what's in your graveyard. Your own mill still gives Mothman counters, and you can get back removal you've already used.
directions.plays_like: Grinds out long games; hard to stop

swaps.why: Mills you 3 when it enters and 3 more when it dies, for 1 mana.
Mills you 3, then can return a creature to your hand when it dies.
Returns any card from your graveyard to your hand, including spent removal.
Gives a card, a Treasure or a 2/2 Zombie whenever cards leave your graveyard.
Mills you 3 when it enters or attacks, and makes a 2/2 Zombie whenever creatures are milled.
Each turn, replay a land and one permanent of each type from your graveyard.

how_to_play.summary: Mill yourself on purpose, then replay creatures and permanents from the graveyard; your own mill still triggers Mothman.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Self-mill: Stitcher's Supplier (3 on enter and on death), Undead Butler (3, then returns a creature when it dies), Sidisi (3 on enter and attack, plus a Zombie when creatures are milled).
Recursion: Muldrotha replays a permanent of each type from your graveyard every turn; Eternal Witness returns any card (including spent removal).
Teval's Judgment gives a card, a Treasure or a Zombie whenever cards leave your graveyard.

sections.title: Tips
points: Mill yourself before casting Muldrotha or Eternal Witness so the best targets are there.
Watch for opponents' graveyard hate (e.g. Bojuka Bog): replay key pieces as soon as they hit your graveyard.

recommendation: Counter Engine fits Mothman best: every mill trigger already gives counters, and these cards make each counter worth more. The removal package covers the deck's biggest weakness in every direction. All three directions stay under €20.
